# Source-only native ALC ownership plan

This implementation has not been compiled or executed. Proof CLI mode remains unavailable. The existing help and malformed-argument controls continue without a wrapper. No compiler, Boogie, solver flag, query, seed, hash implementation, or resource reply is changed.

The API keeps the existing `MainWithWriters` verification path. Construct a single-use `NativeProofSupervisor` with the real solver path/digest, an explicitly delegated cgroup-v2 parent, an existing evidence parent, and Python. A private generated wrapper is pinned to the static source-manifest template digest. The caller must use that exact wrapper in its one explicit `--solver-path`; no environment fallback exists. The first native control set is the true, false, and fuel source fixtures; these are future execution inputs, not proof evidence.

The delegated cgroup must be a private, empty domain group under `/sys/fs/cgroup`, contain no live processes or child groups, and permit the caller to create/delete its own leaf. The supervisor never alters the parent configuration. Missing delegation, pidfds, required permissions or immutable solver identity fails before loading a product. A random exclusive leaf is the ownership boundary: launched wrappers join it before forking, and descendants inherit membership even when reparented or creating new process sessions. This is stronger than a process-tree snapshot. The API assumes the delegated parent is supplied by a trusted CI setup and cannot be written by an unrelated actor; same-UID hostile actors are outside this bounded scratch gate.

Launch admission and closure share a Linux flock. Each launch records the wrapper and solver PID, kernel start time, parent, process group/session, actual solver digest, and exact solver argument array. The solver child waits on a pipe before exec until the supervisor verifies ancestry, exclusive-cgroup membership and pre/post pidfd identity, captures both pidfds, and acknowledges the token. Thus even a short version probe is recorded before it can execute/exit. Every discovered live cgroup member receives a pidfd; no numeric PID or group number alone authorizes a signal. Process groups/sessions are evidence, not a global `killpg` permission.

The wrapper uses binary `os.read`/`os.write`, handles partial/interrupted writes, independently drains stderr, records EOF/OS errors, and logs exact byte streams with read/write counts and SHA-256 digests. It does not decode or modify SMT commands or replies. It executes the exact hashed solver file descriptor, preserving arguments/environment, and its child uses Linux parent-death signaling. Wrapper-internal diagnostics stay in evidence files and never contaminate solver streams. Logging and handshake overhead affect elapsed time, so wall deadlines remain safety caps; no RU correction is permitted.

After CLI completion (including its results/logs), close launch admission, signal only owned non-wrapper pidfds, and allow wrappers to drain streams/reap solvers/exit. Escalate owned solver pidfds when necessary. Forced wrapper termination makes the receipt fail because log completeness is unproven. A cleanup receipt requires nonempty complete launch records, exact read/write stream equality, zero relay failures, zero live captured pidfds, empty membership and `cgroup.events populated 0`; deleting the now-empty leaf closes late-admission races. Missing/changed identity, monitor faults, incomplete receipts or cleanup failures poison the existing host through `Runs` and retain evidence. No unrelated process is signalled.

Normal wrapper exit reaches Boogie `SMTLibProcess.SolverExited` and `DisposeProver`, which removes its own Console.CancelKeyPress handler (pinned source `73a0e214`, `Source/Provers/SMTLib/SMTLibProcess.cs`). This implementation neither edits shared event backing fields nor claims to dispose an uncaptured engine. The actual private scheduler must still be disposed, and the existing long weak reference must become dead before another context starts. If solver shutdown does not permit actual ALC collection, the whole-CLI design is blocked; do not silently weaken unload or detach global handlers.

Pending mandatory controls before enabling proof CLI: compile/API review; cgroup delegation failure; absent/wrong solver/template digest; refused late launch; short probe ownership; partial-write/EOF/stderr/error forwarding; timeout and descendant/reparenting cleanup; pid reuse rejection; incomplete receipt rejection; real native true/false/fuel outcomes; actual context unload and framework witness stability; exact source/toolchain/hash receipts. Historical short-lived descendants that vanish between scans are not individually enumerated; authoritative cgroup emptiness establishes the live-process cleanup boundary. Stream equality currently authenticates forwarding, not complete SMT-query/RU denominators. Full native-query/resource comparisons and broader P1 gates remain separate work.
